lines.text: Two friends, two different money swaps, and two clues.
lines.caption: Two friends, two different money swaps, and two clues.

lines.text: Can we find how much money they have together? Let's draw it out!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this with bars.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this with bars.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: If Ali gives Bea twenty percent of his money, they will have the same amount.
lines.caption: If Ali gives Bea twenty percent of his money, they will have the same amount.

lines.text: If instead Bea gives Ali ten dollars, Ali will have twice as much as Bea.
lines.caption: If instead Bea gives Ali ten dollars, Ali will have twice as much as Bea.

lines.text: How many dollars do our two friends, Ali and Bea, have together?
lines.caption: How many dollars do our two friends, Ali and Bea, have together?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: There are two clues. The word instead means each one starts fresh, from the same amounts again.
lines.caption: There are two clues. The word instead means each one starts fresh, from the same amounts again.

lines.text: We want the total: Ali's money plus Bea's money.
lines.caption: We want the total: Ali's money plus Bea's money.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's draw a bar model.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's draw a bar model.

lines.text: Twenty percent is one fifth. So split Ali's money into five equal parts.
lines.caption: Twenty percent is one fifth. So split Ali's money into five equal parts.

lines.text: Clue one: Ali gives one part to Bea. Now Ali has four parts.
lines.caption: Clue one: Ali gives one part to Bea. Now Ali has four parts.

lines.text: They have the same amount, so Bea now has four parts too.
lines.caption: They have the same amount, so Bea now has four parts too.

lines.text: One of those parts was Ali's gift. So Bea started with three parts.
lines.caption: One of those parts was Ali's gift. So Bea started with three parts.

lines.text: Clue two, starting fresh: Bea gives Ali ten dollars.
lines.caption: Clue two, starting fresh: Bea gives Ali ten dollars.

lines.text: After the swap, Ali has five parts plus ten, and Bea has three parts minus ten.
lines.caption: After the swap, Ali has five parts plus ten, and Bea has three parts minus ten.

lines.text: Twice Bea's money is six parts, minus twenty dollars.
lines.caption: Twice Bea's money is six parts, minus twenty dollars.

lines.text: Ali has twice as much, so five parts plus ten equals six parts minus twenty.
lines.caption: Ali has twice as much, so five parts plus ten equals six parts minus twenty.

lines.text: Take five parts from both sides. One part minus twenty is ten.
lines.caption: Take five parts from both sides. One part minus twenty is ten.

lines.text: So one part is thirty dollars.
lines.caption: So one part is thirty dollars.

lines.text: So Ali has five parts, one hundred fifty dollars, and Bea has three parts, ninety dollars.
lines.caption: So Ali has five parts, one hundred fifty dollars, and Bea has three parts, ninety dollars.

lines.text: Together, that's two hundred forty dollars. Choice D!
lines.caption: Together, that's two hundred forty dollars. Choice D!

lines.text: Let's check clue one. Twenty percent of one hundred fifty is thirty.
lines.caption: Let's check clue one. Twenty percent of one hundred fifty is thirty.

lines.text: Ali keeps one hundred twenty, and Bea ends up with one hundred twenty.
lines.caption: Ali keeps one hundred twenty, and Bea ends up with one hundred twenty.

lines.text: Clue two: Ali ends with one hundred sixty, and Bea drops to eighty.
lines.caption: Clue two: Ali ends with one hundred sixty, and Bea drops to eighty.

lines.text: One hundred sixty is twice eighty. Both clues work!
lines.caption: One hundred sixty is twice eighty. Both clues work!

lines.text: Here's another way. Use letters: a for Ali's dollars and b for Bea's.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Use letters: a for Ali's dollars and b for Bea's.

lines.text: Clue one: a minus a fifth of a equals b plus a fifth of a.
lines.caption: Clue one: a minus a fifth of a equals b plus a fifth of a.

lines.text: So b is a minus two fifths of a. That's three fifths of a.
lines.caption: So b is a minus two fifths of a. That's three fifths of a.

lines.text: Clue two: a plus ten equals two times, b minus ten.
lines.caption: Clue two: a plus ten equals two times, b minus ten.

lines.text: That's six fifths of a, minus twenty.
lines.caption: That's six fifths of a, minus twenty.

lines.text: So one fifth of a is thirty. Then a is one hundred fifty, and b is ninety. Same answer!
lines.caption: So one fifth of a is thirty. Then a is one hundred fifty, and b is ninety. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the parts don't come out even, letters still work.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the parts don't come out even, letters still work.

lines.text: Now the traps. Choices A and B, ninety and one hundred fifty, are each person alone.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Choices A and B, ninety and one hundred fifty, are each person alone.

lines.text: Choice E, three hundred, doubles Ali's money instead of adding Bea's.
lines.caption: Choice E, three hundred, doubles Ali's money instead of adding Bea's.
